<STRUCT_0001>
Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme. We denote <MATH_0002> the
category of quasi-coherent <MATH_0003>-modules as defined in
Modules, Definition <REF_0001>.
We have seen in
Section <REF_0002>
that the category <MATH_0004> has a lot of good properties
when <MATH_0005> is affine. Since the property of being quasi-coherent is
local on <MATH_0006>, these properties are inherited by the category
of quasi-coherent sheaves on any scheme <MATH_0007>. We enumerate them here.
<STRUCT_0002>
<STRUCT_0003> A sheaf of <MATH_0008>-modules <MATH_0009> is
quasi-coherent if and only if the restriction of <MATH_0010>
to each affine open <MATH_0011> is of the form
<MATH_0012> for some <MATH_0013>-module <MATH_0014>.
<STRUCT_0004> A sheaf of <MATH_0015>-modules <MATH_0016> is
quasi-coherent if and only if the restriction of <MATH_0017>
to each of the members of an affine open covering is quasi-coherent.
<STRUCT_0005> Any direct sum of quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent.
<STRUCT_0006> Any colimit of quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent.
<STRUCT_0007>
<LOCKED_0001>
The kernel and cokernel of a morphism of quasi-coherent sheaves
is quasi-coherent.
<STRUCT_0008> Given a short exact sequence of <MATH_0018>-modules
<MATH_0019>
if two out of three are quasi-coherent so is the third.
<STRUCT_0009> Given a morphism of schemes <MATH_0020> the pullback
of a quasi-coherent <MATH_0021>-module is a quasi-coherent
<MATH_0022>-module. See
Modules, Lemma <REF_0003>.
<STRUCT_0010> Given two quasi-coherent <MATH_0023>-modules
the tensor product is quasi-coherent, see
Modules, Lemma <REF_0004>.
<STRUCT_0011> Given a quasi-coherent <MATH_0024>-module <MATH_0025>
the tensor, symmetric and exterior algebras on <MATH_0026>
are quasi-coherent, see
Modules, Lemma <REF_0005>.
<STRUCT_0012> Given two quasi-coherent <MATH_0027>-modules
<MATH_0028>, <MATH_0029> such that <MATH_0030>
is of finite presentation, then the internal hom
<MATH_0031>
is quasi-coherent, see
Modules, Lemma <REF_0006>
and (<REF_0007>) above.
